title: Fixing Ephemeral Port Exhaustion with Connection Pooling
prompt: Your high-throughput aggregator microservice (Python `requests` / Java `RestTemplate` on Kubernetes Linux nodes) calls an internal pricing service at 1,500 RPS per pod. During peak traffic, pods begin throwing `Cannot assign requested address (EADDRNOTAVAIL)` and `BindException` while CPU is only 35%. `ss -tan state time-wait | wc -l` reveals 28,200+ sockets stuck in `TIME_WAIT` against the same `10.96.45.12:8080` destination IP:port. Identify why ports exhausted at 1,500 RPS, fix the HTTP client architecture, and apply safe Linux/Kubernetes mitigations.

spark.summary: Calling a single Kubernetes ClusterIP at 1,500 RPS without HTTP keep-alive opens a new TCP socket per request and leaves it in 60s TIME_WAIT, exhausting all 28,232 Linux ephemeral ports in ~18 seconds; persistent connection pooling drops TIME_WAIT sockets below 200.
spark.keyTakeaway: When a single bottleneck threatens end-to-end availability, reuse TCP/TLS sockets via a singleton HTTP keep-alive connection pool (reducing ephemeral ports from 28,200+ to < 200), and never enable tcp_tw_recycle behind Kubernetes NAT.

explanation.foundation: Linux allocates outbound client ports from `ip_local_port_range = 32768..60999` (**28,232** ports).

learningJourney.title: What happens when every request creates a fresh TCP socket

explanation.foundation: Opening and closing a TCP socket per outbound call causes three failures:
explanation.core:
1. **4-Tuple Exhaustion**: Because `(dst_ip, dst_port)` is fixed to `10.96.45.12:8080`, all `28,232` `(src_ip, src_port)` pairs lock in `TIME_WAIT`.
2. **TCP/TLS Handshake Tax**: Every call pays 1–2 extra RTTs for TCP + TLS handshakes.
3. **Unsafe Kernel Hacks**: Enabling deprecated `tcp_tw_recycle` breaks clients behind NAT / `kube-proxy`.

learningJourney.markdownContent:
```python
import httpx

# Process-wide singleton HTTP/1.1 + HTTP/2 keep-alive pool (reused across all requests)
limits = httpx.Limits(
    max_connections=200,
    max_keepalive_connections=150,
    keepalive_expiry=30.0,  # strictly < upstream server idle timeout (e.g. 60s)
)
pricing_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
    base_url="http://pricing-service.internal:8080",
    limits=limits,
    http2=True,
    timeout=httpx.Timeout(2.0, connect=0.2),
)
```
